title: Suggestion Gateway: approval lattice, canary lanes, and rollback circuit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a "Suggestion Gateway" service to safely auto-apply Optimize suggestions (batching, caching, quantization hints) with multi-dimensional safety controls. The Gateway must act as a middleware/controller that validates incoming suggestions, runs deterministic dry-runs against a replay dataset, places suggestions into canary lanes, orchestrates an approval lattice for manual/automated signoffs, and implements an automatic rollback circuit when guardrail metrics regress. This reduces manual toil while maintaining predictable latency/cost trade-offs for customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Gateway accepts Optimize suggestion payloads and stores immutable proposal bundle with metadata (model, route, config diffs, suggested metrics).
2) Proposal payloads run a dry-run against the configured replay set (same token distribution) and produce a compare report (latency P50/P95, tok/sec, error rate, cost delta). Dry-run must complete within 10 minutes for standard sets.
3) Canary lanes created automatically: default lane -> 0.5% traffic for 1 hour -> 2% for 3 hours -> 10% for 24 hours. Canary progression must be gated by metric checks.
4) Approval lattice implemented: can express required approvers from roles (pm, infra-sre, privacy) and allow automated approval if all automated checks pass and no manual approvers are configured.
5) Automatic rollback circuit: if after promotion any metric crosses threshold (latency P95 +30% absolute, error rate +1% absolute, cost increase >15% without commensurate latency decrease), system reverts to previous config and opens an incident.
6) Console UX: proposal page with diff view, replay report, canary status, approval history, and one-click manual rollback.
7) Observability: proposal-level tracing, per-candidate metrics exported to Dashboard (proposal/<id>) and audit logs stored for 1 year.
8) Tests: unit/integration tests for state transitions, and end-to-end test that simulates replay -> canary -> promote -> rollback.
technical_notes:
Architecture: lightweight controller service (suggestion-gateway) with the following components:
- Validator: schema checks, model-compatibility matrix, quantization safe flags.
- Replayer: schedules dry-run jobs on a reduced cluster using the customer's replay dataset. Uses the runtime sandbox for deterministic KV/cache priming.
- Canary router: integrates with serving runtime router to split a small percentage of real traffic to a candidate config. Uses session affinity to avoid mixing sessions.
- Gate evaluator: continuous metrics evaluator that queries Prometheus/Tracing to decide promotions or rollbacks.
- Approval Lattice: role-based approval state machine persisted in proposal metadata; supports conditional auto-approve rules.
- Rollback Circuit: circuit module that can trigger immediate revert and create an incident (integrates with PagerDuty and Console incident UI).
Deployment considerations: Gateway runs in control plane for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private/VPC we ship an agent that can perform replays locally and apply on a customer-managed control plane.
Trade-offs and decisions recorded:
- We opted for traffic-based canary rather than CPU-based because inference latency/cost are more sensitive to per-request behavior.
- Dry-run on reduced cluster introduces some measurement noise; to mitigate, we compute 95% CI and require results to be significant at p<0.05 for promotion.
- We will start with a conservative default canary cadence and make it tunable per-customer.

playbook: If auto-rollback triggers: 1) Notify on #incidents and PagerDuty, 2) Open proposal and mark failed step, 3) Run immediate revert job if not already reverted, 4) Start post-mortem template (link in Confluence)
Manual-override: SRE or PM can pause canary progression via Console -> Proposal -> Pause. Changes must be logged with explanation.
For Private deployments: Operator runs local replay job and approves in local Console before the Gateway applies changes to serving plane. Document operator checklist in Confluence.
